sentences.text:
Smt. Babita vs Yogendra Singh on 2 September, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:24593
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 2 nd Of September, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 7098 of 2019
 Smt. Babita And Others
 Versus
 Yogendra Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Jagdish Baheti - Advocate with Shri Prashant Jai
 the appellants.
 Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate with Shri Bhashkar
 Advocate for the respondent [R-3].
 Order

Appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") being aggrieved by the award dated 26.06.2019 passed in Claim Case No.14/2019 challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground of improper assessment of income of deceased Dinesh.
02.
The factum of liability of the Insurance Company due to death in the accident by insured vehicle is not under dispute.

03. Short facts of the case are that on 06.04.2017, the deceased Kanchanbai was going with her son Dinesh on motorcycle to Village Dudlai, when they reached near Bhaursa square at Indore-Bhopal highway, respondent No.2 came driving Tavera car bearing registration No.MP-09- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24593 2 MA-7098-2019 BD-4434 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of Dinesh because of which both Dinesh and Kanchanbai fell from the motorcycle and got dragged to some distance.
Kanchanbai died while on the way to the hospital and Dinesh died at the spot itself.
An FIR was registered under Section 279, 337 and 304-A of IPC.
The appellants filed claim petitions before the Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of MV Act claiming compensation for the death of Dinesh.
The Claims Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total sum of Rs.11,45,200/- to the appellants.
04. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal has incorrectly assessed the income of the deceased.

He while referring to the documents regarding the criminal case, submits that it has clearly come on record that the deceased Dinesh was maintaining a motorcycle thus,
Smt. Babita vs Yogendra Singh on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77711412/
1 looking to his living standard he should be treated as skilled labour and accordingly his incomes should have been assessed by the claims tribunal.

He further submits that the amount of consortium has been awarded only to the wife of the deceased although two minor children and father of the deceased were also before the claims tribunal as claimants and in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782 , all of them were entitled for compensation under head of consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from this he also submits that deduction under the head of personal expenses at 1/3rd is also not correct in view of the fact that there were four claimants i.e. two children, one wife and father thus 1/4th should have been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24593 3 MA-7098-2019 deducted.
Therefore, he prays for enhancement of the compensation.

05. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits by referring to the impugned award that even the wife of the deceased in her statement as PW-1 stated that the deceased was earning Rs. 5,800/- pm, but the claims tribunal after concluding that her evidence was not reliable assessed the income of the deceased on notional basis at Rs. 6,000/- pm.

Thus, he submits that even after considering the evidence of the claimants as believable still the income would have been Rs.
5,800/-.
As regards deduction he submits that the father was not dependent on the income of the deceased as he was owning the agricultural land and was earning for himself.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
06. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

07. It is seen from the findings recorded by the claims tribunal as well as on perusal of the statement of Babita Bai (PW-1) that she herself has stated that her husband was earning Rs. 5,800/- but the claims tribunal has not believed the same.
Apart from this, there is no other material to establish that the deceased was a skilled labour.
In such circumstances, this Court does not find any fault in the conclusion of the claims tribunal in treating the deceased as an unskilled labour.
However, at the relevant time the minimum wages for unskilled labour were Rs. 7,125/-.

As such the income of the deceased is modified to Rs. 7125/-.
08.

As regards the consortium considering the fact that four claimants are wife, two children and father of the deceased they all are entitled for spousal, parental and filial consortium in view of the law laid down by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24593 4 MA-7098-2019 Apex Court in the case of Magma (supra) as such, all four are awarded an amount of Rs. 40,000/- each totaling to Rs.1,60,000/-, as the amount of Rs. 40,000/- has already been awarded to wife, thus an additional amount of Rs. 1,20,000/- has to be paid.

09. After above modification in the income of the deceased, the amount under the head of loss of dependency would come to Rs.12,76,800/- and after deducting the already awarded amount the total payable amount would now come to Rs. 3,21,600/- (including consortium of Rs.1,20,000/-).
This amount shall be paid to the appellants over and above the amount already awarded by claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the Claims Tribunal.
